channel.title: PaddySpeaks — all essays
channel.description: Essays on philosophy, technology, AI and personal growth by Paddy Iyer.

item.title: AI Is Looking For You
item.description: An interactive story in nine scenes about how professional discovery is changing: an agent scanning three fictional careers in fifteen seconds, the same person described two ways, the beautiful portfolio that describes nothing, the five signals a machine needs, the digital shadow that arrives before you do, and a search box where you can brief the agent yourself.

item.title: The Job Posting Is Not the Job
item.description: A visual field guide to the 2026 hiring market. Twelve scenes: why 244 applications now reach one triaging recruiter, a four-minute autopsy that proves whether a job exists, the org chart hiding behind every posting, the six-rung climb from stranger to advocate, the anatomy of a message that gets answered, and the thirty minutes a day that beat six hours of Easy Apply.

item.title: Can You Really Afford the Bay Area?
item.description: A seventeen-slide visual essay: one four-bedroom house in Santa Clara County followed from 1960 to 2026 — Proposition 13, the mortgage-rate myth, the $200,000 paradox, the RSU economy, AI and the 30-year mortgage — and why wealth may be better measured in years of freedom than in square feet.

item.title: The Interview Room
item.description: A fictional screenplay in fifteen acts. Alex Morgan runs escalation engineering at Northstar Data Platforms; Jordan Lee has twenty-two years behind them. Spark plans, data skew, JVM garbage collection, heap dumps, driver versus executor OOM, small-file lakehouses, streaming backlogs, an upgrade regression — and the questions behind the questions.

item.title: The Subject Nobody Taught
item.description: Fourteen years of school. Four of college. Zero classes on the one thing you use every single day. A visual essay on the missing curriculum, the phrases parents pass down instead of principles, what $500 a month actually becomes over thirty years, and why rich flaunts while wealthy compounds.

item.title: Don’t Be Too Nice
item.description: Steve Jobs gave Indra Nooyi three hours and one blunt instruction. Most people hear it as permission to be a jerk. It isn't — four instructions, ten takeaways for work and life, and why the Bhagavad Gita's nishkama karma never told you to be a doormat.

item.title: Consequences Don’t Transfer
item.description: They gave the advice. You threw the mud on your own head. Four case files, a double-entry ledger of who books the credit and who books the debit, five reasons free counsel is systematically — not occasionally — bad, and a six-question test for how much of your decision an adviser is structurally able to carry.

item.title: The Feed Is Winning. Your Career Isn’t.
item.description: Alex opens LinkedIn and closes it. He opens CareerOS and keeps reading. Same data both times — the only difference is what the software was told to maximize. A design spec, an interactive prototype, and an actual definition of Professional Intelligence.

item.title: Your AI Is Brilliant. Then the Bill Arrives.
item.description: A plain-English and technical guide to what really drives enterprise Gen AI costs — tokens, context windows, RAG, agent loops — and how to control them without starving your model of the tokens that actually matter.

item.title: AI-Native Software Development: Best Practices for Building Without Breaking the Flow
item.description: AI-assisted development isn't about typing code faster. It's about preserving context, standardizing knowledge, and handing work off cleanly across people, tools, and time zones. A practical framework for building institutional memory around AI — with a reusable skill, a full EOB handoff prompt, and a Context → Plan → Build → Verify → Record → Handoff → Learn loop.

item.title: What's Your Seatbelt? What's Your Parachute?
item.description: One keeps you steady through turbulence you didn't choose. The other decides how you land when the engine actually fails. A visual essay with a side-by-side comparison and a timeline of when each one matters.

item.title: From Hero to Zero — and Back Again
item.description: The crowd's opinion of you can flip in a single news cycle — hero, then zero, then hero again, same person the whole time. What the Buddhist eight worldly winds, Kipling, and the Bhagavad Gita each say about a self-worth that isn't a popularity contest. A visual essay.

item.title: The Equidistance Trap — Why Perfect Information Doesn't Break a Tie
item.description: A 14th-century logic puzzle explains why analysis paralysis in careers, relationships, health, and admissions decisions never resolves with more data — and what Stoicism, Buddhism, Taoism, the Gita, and decision science each independently landed on as the fix. A visual essay.

item.title: You Don't Have to Carry Yesterday Into Tomorrow
item.description: Old wounds don't need to be forgotten. They need to stop being carried. The Buddhist parable of the second arrow, the psychology of rumination, and what letting go actually looks like. A visual essay.

item.title: Designing DigiCert — PKI, X.509 Certificates & Kubernetes at Scale
item.description: From the byte layout of an X.509 cert to a CA issuing a million certs a day on Kubernetes — what a certificate is, where it lives (macOS Keychain, Windows Store, JVM cacerts, K8s Secrets), how TLS handshakes work, and how cert-manager, SPIFFE/SPIRE, and Istio mTLS replace manual PKI at cloud scale.

item.title: Designing Google Calendar — Recurrence, Time Zones & Free/Busy, in Schema, SQL & Python
item.description: One row can mean infinite meetings, and a single daylight-saving change can silently move a million standups. The recurrence-and-exceptions data model, the free/busy bitmap index, and the change-stream pipeline — written out in DDL, SQL and Python rather than boxes and arrows.

item.title: Prodigy or Reincarnation?
item.description: Vaibhav Suryavanshi at 14, Mozart at 5, Sachin at 16, Magnus Carlsen at 13 — talent that arrives fully formed from unremarkable families. Genetic jackpot, or the Bhagavad Gita's verse 6.43, a soul resuming an unfinished journey? A visual, infographic-led essay: Darwin versus Dharma.

item.title: Data Modeling for the Modern Warehouse
item.description: A practitioner's field guide — slowly changing dimensions, the three fact-table grains, factless facts, One Big Table, Data Vault, change data capture, the medallion architecture, and what housekeeping each cloud warehouse actually needs.

item.title: The Uber Algorithm — 30 Million Trips a Day, Explained in SQL & Python
item.description: A pre-emptive interview handbook for aspiring Data Architects and Data Engineers: dispatch, surge, ETA, routing, and pickup sequencing — with the data plumbing made visible in SQL, Python, and visual data.

item.title: Introduction to Data Engineering — 100 SQL & Python Interview Questions
item.description: An introduction to the discipline plus a graduated 100-question practice bank: 50 SQL + 50 Python problems on a realistic e-commerce dataset, ordered from SELECT * to recursive CTEs, from pd.read_csv to PySpark broadcast joins.
